newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait plans 649 new oil wells to boost output.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait plans 649 new oil wells to boost output.

text.p: Kuwait plans to drill 649 new wells to raise oil production capacity in anticipation of an OPEC quota of three million bpd in the next century, Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi said in remarks published on Sunday.

"Production, in accordance with (OPEC) ceiling, will be increased from two million (bpd) to 2.4 million in the year 2000 and to three million (afterwards)," al-Seyassah daily quoted Mazeedi as telling parliament on Saturday.

Kuwait has repeatedly said it deserves a higher OPEC quota, possibly a 200,000 barrel per day (bpd) increase over the current two million bpd, but officials say a formal request will be made at the right time.
The tiny Gulf Arab state, which controls about 10 percent of the world's proven crude reserves, has a current production capacity of 2.5 million bpd. Production peaked at three million bpd in 1973.

"There are plans to determine an increase in the capacity of gathering centres and other programmes to drill 649 oil wells, of which some would be production wells and others would be injection wells," added the minister.
